local_checks.result: run-host-rows.py (tests/run-host-rows.py) selects rows with kind=host, the chosen host and verdict=pending. It runs each command cell, or the notes file's run cell, with ["bash", "-lc", shell], env = os.environ plus HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM, cwd the worktree root, stdin closed and a per-row timeout (run_row), then writes observed, verdict and ts back into the table. check-tables.py only validates table shape. Nothing in the repository or CI invokes either. At this head every one of the 31 host rows in the ten tables is already judged (0 pending, per the parent's read of the cells), and the notes file is not in the tree, so the published copy starts nothing. The command cells were produced by a unit (U274) whose output the coordinator copies into its own store, and the coordinator chooses when to run the executor. Same principal at run time, recorded as a hardening note.

hardening_notes: tests/run-host-rows.py runs table command text with `bash -lc`, the full environment and no sandbox, on whichever host the coordinator runs it. The tables were produced by a worker unit (U274) and copied into the store. A future pending host row runs exactly as written, as do the notes file's run cells. Printing each pending command and requiring a confirmation, or running host rows under the worker seat's srt settings where a row does not need the host, would keep a worker-authored row from becoming unsandboxed host execution by default.
